new_items.title: Agents SDK v1.0.0-alpha.2
new_items.summary:
Agents SDK v1.0.0-alpha.2

Highlights

  • Resume conversations and pending approvals across workers with Responses or Codex.
  • Recover supported native Codex command and edit approvals.
  • Configure tool execution hooks and filter available function tools.
  • Opt into Runner text redaction and detailed operation tracing with either provider.
  • Upgrade checkpoint readers before writers. Alpha.2 introduces new persisted state formats.

Install

This GitHub-only preview bundles openai-agents and the native Codex runtime.

Activate a standard CPython 3.10–3.14 virtual environment, then run the single command for your platform. Pip verifies the downloaded wheel against its SHA-256 hash from the release's SHA256SUMS file before installing it.

Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.28+)

python -m pip install --only-binary=:all: "https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.2/openai_agents-1.0.0a2-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl#sha256=1c073472688dfae9ed4b082ad4be3451ceb2cf7913bfb56b1a9af258b63cdf7b"

Linux ARM64 (glibc 2.28+)

python -m pip install --only-binary=:all: "https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.2/openai_agents-1.0.0a2-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl#sha256=fd879e9f013173af52e60a2706133633ef4d1edf6ae1b5899e2f022a26aaba73"

macOS 11+ (Apple silicon)

python -m pip install --only-binary=:all: "https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.2/openai_agents-1.0.0a2-cp310-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl#sha256=4a86bf3c2ffd9018ec05bc3744a3f00898b019007922d0a0640864e4b704129f"

Windows x64

python -m pip install --only-binary=:all: "https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/releases/download/v1.0.0-alpha.2/openai_agents-1.0.0a2-cp310-abi3-win_amd64.whl#sha256=a1b5d648ee998c755f792128c9066260eb8a5ff4c050d1812986834baaf4579f"

To get started, see the Codex examples guide.

Upgrading from v1.0.0-alpha.1

  • Alpha.2 reads alpha.1 RunState schema 1.22 and always writes schema 1.24, even with redaction disabled. Alpha.1 cannot read new snapshots.
  • Protected ResumableSession checkpoints use version 2.

Sessions and approvals

  • Use ResumableSession to persist conversation history and pending approvals together. Supply a ResumableSessionStore with atomic conditional writes or use RedisSessionStore. Protect checkpoint storage and allow one writer per session. See the session guide.
  • On a replacement worker, call session = await ResumableSession.resume(store, session_id) and state = await session.load_state(agent). Recreate config with the appropriate model provider, matching tool declaration and authorization policy, hooks, and redactor. Use CodexProvider for pending native Codex approvals. Approve or reject the original interruption through RunState, then continue with await Runner.run(agent, state, session=session, run_config=config).
  • Native Codex recovery supports one pending direct exec_command or apply_patch approval in one local environment. Restore the same workspace path, permissions, and required hooks. Affected files must match their saved state. Missing required SDK tools or hooks leave approvals pending. Managed native hooks can also stop approval recovery. Keep required hooks enabled. Restored native results enter the conversation's replay history. See the native approval example.
  • After failure or worker loss, inspect the checkpoint and workspace. Reconcile partial edits and other external effects before retrying. Recovery cannot restart terminated commands or recover alpha.1 approvals that ended the model call.

Tool execution

  • Configure RunConfig.tool_execution with ToolExecutionConfig. Experimental prepare_tool_input modifies arguments before approval and execution. prepare_tool_output modifies results after execution. Both support SDK tools with either provider and hooked native Codex tools. Responses-hosted tools execute outside these callbacks.
  • Use prepare_tool_declaration to change or withhold supported function declarations. The Runner rechecks eligibility before execution, including after approval. See the tool hooks example.
  • With input or output hooks configured, sdk_only_tool_hooks=True disables native Codex workspace tools and their approval recovery.
  • Embedded Codex Core rust-v0.166.0 includes a patch blocking native dispatch when any synchronous PreToolUse handler fails or times out. After approval, the replacement worker runs configured on_tool_start callbacks and reuses the approved input without applying prepare_tool_input again. Asynchronous notifications and output hooks cannot prevent an action already started. See the required tool hooks patch.
  • When the manager run is cancelled, active Agent.as_tool() calls get up to 250 ms to clean up. Repeated cancellation does not reset the deadline. Tools that exceed the timeout may continue running and cause side effects or state changes after cancellation returns. #6130

Redaction and tracing

  • Opt into RunConfig.redact_text with your own synchronous callback. It changes recognized text sent to the model and SDK tools, replies, streams, and persisted state. Supply the same callback when continuing protected sessions. Protected runs withhold raw stream events and restrict automatic traces to metadata. Binary media and native Codex operations remain outside its protection. See the redaction guide.
  • Use RunConfig(tracing={"operation_detail": "metadata"}) for operation metadata with either provider. Set "operation_detail" to "content" to capture bounded model inputs and outputs, tool arguments, and available results. Model retries add events to the same model span.
  • Default SDK tracing can expose native Codex results, including file contents, through returned responses or replayed history. Set RunConfig(trace_include_sensitive_data=False) to suppress sensitive trace payloads in every mode. Use RunConfig(tracing_disabled=True) to disable SDK tracing entirely.
  • Install the verified wheel with its [opentelemetry] extra and use OpenTelemetryTracingProcessor to export SDK spans through your application's tracer provider. OpenTelemetry exports payloads only in "content" mode. See the OpenTelemetry setup.

new_items.title: v2.1.331
new_items.summary:
What's changed

  • Added Code Mode support in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS
  • Added oidc.groups_jsonpath to the Claude apps gateway, to read groups from the matching entries of a list of objects with a small subset of JSONPath (RFC 9535)
  • Added an API connectivity section to claude doctor that reports whether the API can be reached, with the HTTP status or the error, or says why it wasn't tested
  • Added a notice when tap-mode voice dictation stops by itself, after 15 seconds without recognized speech or at its 2-minute limit
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION to ask for uncompressed model responses behind a proxy that cuts compressed ones off; not advised yet for self-hosted runners or Remote Control
  • Added CLAUDE_GATEWAY_IDP_CONNECT_BY_HOSTNAME=1 for Claude apps gateways: with oidc.use_proxy: true, sign-in requests hand the proxy an https IdP's hostname even with NO_PROXY set
  • Added gen_ai.usage.*, gen_ai.response.model and gen_ai.operation.name to claude_code.llm_request trace spans; gen_ai.usage.input_tokens includes prompt cache tokens
  • Added optionalDependencies to plugin manifests: plugins that install with the plugin listing them and can be disabled or uninstalled on their own
  • Fixed MCP tool calls hanging for up to 30 minutes on some malformed replies from a local or WebSocket server
  • Fixed PushNotification telling a headless run, such as a scheduled one, that the terminal was active in its first minute, instead of saying whether a mobile push was requested
  • Fixed /install-github-app skipping the repository step after setup warnings when no repository was found, and Esc not going back from its workflow list and sign-in steps
  • Fixed one-line tool results cut with no ellipsis in narrow windows, Markdown stars in the Auto mode tab of /permissions, and a hook's reason to stop a forked skill showing twice
  • Fixed /diff hiding its key hints and not selecting files in windows of 24 to 26 rows, and leaving out files added with git add -N in a repository with no commits
  • Fixed the first-run theme list showing too few themes in short windows, and /usage and other tall screens coming out garbled there
  • Fixed /bug in fullscreen hiding its Yes and No answers behind a long report, and Yes staying out of view in very short windows
  • Fixed /compact and auto-compact sometimes losing part of the conversation summary when the summary quoted certain XML tags
  • Fixed Claude not being told when permission rules on the Agent tool dropped its queued message to a subagent that had already ended
  • Fixed a Remote Control message sometimes showing above the reply that was finishing when it was sent
  • Fixed Stop hooks that read the transcript missing the last reply in Claude Desktop; SubagentStop hooks now wait for it too
  • Fixed turns and subagents failing in cloud sessions, or timing out on long replies elsewhere, when a reply went silent while Claude was still thinking; Claude Code now tries the request once more
  • Fixed Esc and Stop waiting about a minute or more when the contents of a cloud or network file that Claude is reading stall
  • Fixed Code Mode sessions resumed with --resume or --continue in another permission mode losing thinking and the prompt cache; one begun in a mode that asks keeps that mode's limits on scripts
  • Fixed Code Mode sending a request about every second when a ! or slash command was typed while a script was running
  • Fixed an interrupted or failed plugin update leaving a partial plugin folder that later loaded with skills or other components missing (#102186)
  • Windows: Fixed file writes on FAT32 and exFAT drives asking for permission every time in some plugin sessions
  • Fixed Claude failing to read a notebook that has a null output or an error output with no traceback
  • Fixed a rewind deleting files after a restore had failed
  • Fixed auto mode sometimes refusing Claude's call to stop a /loop, which left the next wake-up to fire
  • Fixed a Workflow agent's background shells and MCP servers sometimes being left running after it handed back its report
  • Windows: Fixed /desktop downloading the older Claude Desktop installer, and asking for an update when an older install's folder was left behind
  • Fixed claude plugin install, marketplace add and similar commands hanging with no output when managed settings needed an approval that could not be asked for
  • Fixed a permission rule on a subagent's model, such as Agent(model:*), blocking Claude's follow-up message to a subagent started on this version with no model named
  • Fixed PermissionRequest hooks not saving Skill(name:*) allow rules outside local settings
  • Fixed "Ask your admin" asking to raise your own limit when your team's pooled group budget blocked you, and saying "Request sent" when an admin had approved your request in the last few minutes
  • Fixed Code Mode losing the middle of a long script output; Claude now gets a path to the uncut text (#111373)
  • Fixed hold-to-talk dictation stopping early and losing words when Claude Code was busy
  • Fixed Code Mode with --bare not telling Claude what its scripts can call
  • Fixed a crash when a custom API endpoint returned a tool call with no tool name; the call now fails with an error and the session continues
  • Windows: Fixed a possible crash when the machine is almost out of memory
  • Fixed the CLI freezing on some replies, and quoted text sometimes going missing or showing twice
  • Windows: Fixed Claude Code refusing to start when managed settings in the registry contain non-ASCII characters such as Japanese (#93280)
  • Windows: Fixed Remote Control clients showing no steps for a new subagent
  • Fixed @-mentions written as @file#10-12 attaching the whole file instead of those lines
  • Fixed Claude misreading a pasted artifact invitation link; it now asks you to accept the invitation and paste the artifact's own link
  • Fixed sandboxed Bash commands sometimes failing to start on a full temp disk, for sandboxes whose file rules keep commands out of the temp directory
  • Improved typing speed in screen reader mode, most of all in long sessions
  • Improved start-up time: a session started soon after another no longer waits for the model list, and one outside a git repository without .claude/settings.local.json no longer waits on git
  • Windows: Improved the speed of the first Bash command in a session on machines with no custom shell start-up files
  • Improved the plugin auto-update notice to name plugins it newly installs as dependencies, separately from updated plugins
  • Improved Code Mode tool search to show more of an MCP tool's description, with its limits, formats and defaults
  • Improved the Console sign-in link shown by /login and claude auth login --console: it is now much shorter
  • Improved Claude's list of your artifacts: it now marks web pages, so Claude is less likely to try opening one with the Claude Docs connector
  • Improved the folder trust prompts in short terminals: fullscreen /cd and /add-dir show their choices in fewer rows, and the prompt at launch keeps the folder path in view when it has many warnings
  • Changed the questions for stopping auto-connect in /ide and for /clear, /compact or /rewind in a subagent's view to list Yes first; they still start on No, so Down then Enter now answers No
  • Changed what a PermissionDenied hook's retry: true tells Claude: make the refused call again only if you asked for that call
  • Changed in a future release, on or after November 30, 2026: plugin marketplaces in managed extraKnownMarketplaces will auto-update by default. To opt one out, set "autoUpdate": false on its entry
  • Windows: Changed start-up with managed settings in the registry: check them before upgrading, as an HKLM policy outranks managed-settings.json and a broken value can stop the start
  • [VSCode] Added a warning and a link to the revoke page when you log out and the request to revoke your claude.ai login isn't confirmed
  • [VSCode] Added a notice before sending a very large selection or attached text file, and advice under "Prompt is too long" that names the large part and what to do next
  • [VSCode] Added "Add Cell to Chat" to the notebook cell menu, which attaches a cell with its outputs or error
  • [VSCode] Added "Fix with Claude Code" as a quick fix for errors and warnings and to failed tests in the test peek and the Test Results view, which puts the problem into the chat box
  • [VSCode] Added "Add to Chat" to the right-click menu of changed files in the Source Control view
  • [VSCode] Added "Resolve Merge Conflicts" to the editor title of a file with merge conflicts and to the Merge Changes group in Source Control
  • [VSCode] Fixed raw tags for selected code under a reworded prompt, the mode button flashing Manual, the slash menu hiding its highlighted row, a broken sign-in image, and a blinking Accept/Reject bar
  • [VSCode] Fixed a forked conversation overwriting the original conversation's plan file; a fork or rewind that can't copy the plan now shows a warning
  • [VSCode] Fixed voice dictation saying no speech was recognized when its connection closed or never opened; it now says the connection was lost or couldn't connect
  • [VSCode] Fixed an unsent side question being lost when its panel closes
  • [VSCode] Fixed Escape stopping Claude after renaming a session, and typing going nowhere after closing the session history with Escape
  • [VSCode] Fixed Rename, Mark as Unread and Add to Group saying "still connecting" on a tab that resumed a session from its history
  • [VSCode] Fixed wide tables and long paths cut off, long errors hiding their close button, errors out of view in the Add MCP server form and Chrome dialog, and plugin pictures ignoring the editor theme
  • [VSCode] Fixed later prompts and the message box covering the Rewind code dialog, and focus jumping from "Never mind" to "Rewind" when it finishes checking files
  • [VSCode] Fixed the command menu keeping an earlier match highlighted while you type more in its filter, so Enter could run the wrong row
  • [VSCode] Fixed the @ menu showing "No files found" before its first search results arrived, or when it couldn't search all files of a very large workspace, which it now says
  • [VSCode] Fixed Escape stopping Claude at a Remove or Delete confirmation in MCP, Hooks and Memory dialogs, on a side question panel's button or link, and on the Bookmarks button with its panel open
  • [VSCode] Fixed empty boxes showing instead of the + and − signs in diffs (#73069)
  • [VSCode] Fixed the chat no longer following Claude's reply after the panel was resized, or hidden and shown again
  • [VSCode] Fixed a chat left in bypass permissions mode reopening in Auto mode instead of your initial permission mode when settings disable bypass
  • [VSCode] Fixed the chat panel freezing on some CSS code blocks and diffs
  • [VSCode] Fixed the context usage indicator disappearing after an API error, "Prompt is too long", or a slash command
  • [VSCode] Fixed a message queued behind a queued /clear being lost
  • [VSCode] Fixed Manage Plugins losing its search box or showing no message when a search has no match, and not saying that the list of available plugins failed to load
  • [VSCode] Fixed proposed changes to notebooks and files with a custom editor opening in a tab with no Accept or Reject that stayed open after the answer
  • [VSCode] Fixed the spend limit message telling Team and Enterprise members to run /usage-credits, which can't send a request to their admin from the panel
  • [VSCode] Fixed a written message being wiped by Tab on a command in the "/" button's menu or by a click on an onboarding suggestion
  • [VSCode] Fixed Claude continuing to edit files after you rewind code while it is working
  • [VSCode] Fixed typed text being lost after /tasks, /copy, /export, a skipped /feedback, or /plan while already in plan mode
  • [VSCode] Fixed the question card dropping a typed "Other" answer on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, and sending the word "Other" when nothing was typed
  • [VSCode] Fixed the panel showing "Something went wrong" for a conversation in which a gateway sent a tool call with no name
  • [VSCode] Fixed unsaved changes being missed, and Claude's edit being overwritten by the next save, in a folder opened through a symlink
  • [VSCode] Fixed @-mentions attaching nothing, or another file of the same name, after Claude changed folders with cd
  • [VSCode] Fixed the arrow keys replacing typed text with an old prompt while selecting, and dropping edits to a recalled prompt
  • [VSCode] Fixed an @-mention added while a permission prompt was open being lost
  • [VSCode] Fixed shortcuts such as Ctrl+1, Alt+1 or Ctrl+Space answering an open dialog, which could restore files in the rewind confirmation or switch the git branch
  • [VSCode] Fixed prompts that start with a file path or code comment being sent without the selected code and having no fork or rewind menu
  • [VSCode] Fixed file links in the chat ignoring your editor associations for files in the workspace, except notebooks (#81482)
  • [VSCode] Fixed selected lines staying attached to your next message after their file's tab was closed
  • [VSCode] Fixed new sessions starting in Edit automatically after pressing Shift+Tab through it to reach Plan mode
  • [VSCode] Fixed an edited command on the permission prompt running without the line breaks that were typed or pasted into it
  • [VSCode] Fixed a newly opened Claude tab not focusing its message box, or taking the keyboard late from the terminal or command palette and sending the typed text as a prompt
  • [VSCode] Fixed Alt+K line ranges such as @app.ts#5-10 sending the whole file, or its first 2,000 lines, instead of the selected lines
  • [VSCode] Fixed diff tabs opening out of order when several subagents wait for approval, and a later edit to the same file cancelling an earlier one
  • [VSCode] Fixed Enter rewriting a message or running a menu action when a /word such as the path /api stands beside other text, and running a typed slash command without its arguments
  • [VSCode] Fixed Electron apps and extension tests failing to start from Claude, a hook or an MCP server; a wrapper, hook or server that runs VS Code as Node must now set ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1
  • [VSCode] Fixed Claude not being told when you reject part of a proposed edit or change it in the diff view before accepting
  • [VSCode] Fixed Escape on a permission prompt sending a half-typed instruction to Claude instead of cancelling
  • [VSCode] Fixed Ctrl+J and Ctrl+O in the chat also opening VS Code's terminal or Open File dialog on Windows and Linux
  • [VSCode] Fixed the @ menu inserting the wrong file on a quick Tab or Enter, and Enter not sending a prompt that ends in an @word with no matching file
  • [VSCode] Fixed new Claude tabs staying blank and the side bar failing to load after closing a tab while Claude was still starting
  • [VSCode] Fixed a quick double click in the panel pressing a button or row that appeared after the first click, or starting a second compaction from the context usage circle
  • [VSCode] Fixed switching models failing with "Settings file is not valid JSON" when settings.json is empty or starts with a byte order mark
  • [VSCode] Fixed memory growing with each fork or rewind of a long conversation until the window was reloaded
  • [VSCode] Fixed plan comments not showing on the plan approval card in Focus view
  • [VSCode] Fixed file links without a line number moving the cursor of an open file to line 1
  • [VSCode] Fixed a missing notification when a conversation running behind another one in the same panel needs a permission or an answer

  • [VSCode] Fixed proposed diffs showing and saving garbled non-ASCII text when files.encoding is not UTF-8
  • [VSCode] Fixed approved edits and writes saving right-to-left marks as literal \u200F escapes on lines with Hebrew, Arabic or Persian text
  • [VSCode] Fixed a model pick being ignored for the next message when Claude's process had ended or was still starting
  • [VSCode] Fixed Rewind showing "No active session" after Claude's process had ended
  • [VSCode] Fixed typing @ leaving a helper process running per tab when no browser is connected, except when Claude in Chrome's service can't be reached
  • [VSCode] Fixed the session list opening every transcript at once, which stalled the editor's extensions and could leave sessions out in projects with many sessions
  • [VSCode] Improved the time to the first reply in a new folder when the Python extension is installed and the folder has no Python
  • [VSCode] Improved the sign-in screen to say when it opened because a request was refused
  • [VSCode] Improved the speed of opening, restoring and switching back to long conversations, most of all with many file edits or where git is slow
  • [VSCode] Improved responsiveness in long chats: smooth typing and large file writes while a reply streams, faster permission prompts, and far less freezing on send with accessibility support on
  • [VSCode] Improved startup and memory use: the panel and new chat tabs open faster, a first message in a new tab is answered sooner, and on Pro and Max plans the folder trust dialog comes up sooner
  • [VSCode] Improved speed in remote windows (SSH, WSL, containers): the panel starts, replies appear and sessions reopen faster
  • [VSCode] Improved the time to a response for the first message after a chat has been idle for a few minutes on a machine that is low on memory
  • [VSCode] Improved how fast chats start, open from history and come back after a restart on slow or antivirus-scanned disks
  • [VSCode] Improved how fast diffs appear in reopened conversations, and removed diff menu entries that did not work
  • [VSCode] Improved the @ file menu to list the files of open editor tabs first, the most recently used on top
  • [VSCode] Changed saving a proposed diff to accept it only after you click or type in its proposed (right) side; a notification says when a save is refused or a close with Save applies nothing
  • [VSCode] Changed diffs from a terminal session to open without moving keyboard focus, and beside a file with unsaved changes; to answer, click Accept or use the terminal
  • [VSCode] Changed permission cards to show only Yes and No when allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly is set and the card would offer an allow rule; key 2 on those cards now answers No
  • [VSCode] Changed a Claude tab to ignore Enter and show a notice when its Find box has lost the keyboard

new_items.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
new_items.summary: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects in an image and predict the relationships between them. The standard PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet settings show how much performance drops without ground-truth boxes and labels, but not where or why a model fails. Knowing this would allow fixing a model where it fails, without retraining. We propose RoHa-SGG (Root-cause-guided Harness optimization for SGG), which extends agentic harness optimization to SGG. It optimizes the harness, the inference code around a frozen SGG model. RoHa-SGG has two main LLM agents. A root-cause analysis (RCA) agent finds the components where the model fails and diagnoses why, and a proposer agent searches for a harness that fixes these causes. We evaluate RoHa-SGG on Visual Genome and PSG with representative two-stage, one-stage, and multimodal-LLM SGG models. The analysis shows that the components where ground-truth triplets are lost differ across models and datasets. RoHa-SGG improves every metric on all five model-dataset combinations. Graph-constrained R@100 and mR@100 rise by up to 15.8 and 26.4 points for the multimodal LLM and by up to 3.6 and 10.1 points for the two-stage and one-stage models. With root-cause guidance, the harness search reaches the final score of an unguided search up to three times faster.

new_items.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
new_items.summary: Multi-agent systems for scientific claim verification increasingly rely on role-structured LLM debate to pressure-test hypotheses. However, when debating agents are instantiated from the same underlying base model, they share identical latent representations, making self-critique bias structurally inevitable. Static fixed-iteration protocols compound this by either halting prematurely before evidence stabilizes or wasting inference compute after convergence. We present \sys{}, a multi-agent research verification framework that addresses both failure modes. First, we introduce an asymmetric role architecture comprising an Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator with opposing epistemic directives, producing significantly lower role-embedding similarity (0.852 vs.\ 0.918 for symmetric Multi-Agent Debate [MAD], $p = 5.82 \times 10^{-8}$) and surfacing more contested claims (22.0\% vs.\ 15.4\%). Second, we propose the Belief-Delta ($\DB$) convergence criterion, an evidence-grounded stopping rule that eliminates over-iteration (0.0\% vs.\ 62.5\% for Fixed-$3$) while cutting LLM calls by 2.4$\times$. Third, each supported claim is anchored to a verbatim literature snippet audited by an independent NLI classifier, achieving a 21.7\% hallucination rate (comparable to 25.9\% for a Self-Refine critic, $p = 0.61$) while establishing auditable evidence grounding. Across 200 runs on 40 research hypotheses evaluated with DeepSeek-R1-32B, \sys{} balances compute efficiency with rigorous epistemic verification.

new_items.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
new_items.summary: Beznau Unit 1 in Switzerland, in operation since 1969, is the most experienced nuclear reactor still running worldwide. Five decades of incremental modernization have left its monitoring systems, alarm logs, variable catalogs, technical specifications and investigation reports in separate silos that were never designed to be queried together. As a result, investigating a core instrumentation anomaly means slow, manual gathering of knowledge scattered across databases, documents, and experienced colleagues. We present a hierarchical multi-agent assistant built on large language models (LLMs) to support these investigations and reduce the need for tedious manual searches in SAP systems. An orchestrating agent breaks down an engineer's question and hands the parts to specialized sub-agents, each with read-only access to one source. Domain expertise is written as natural-language procedures that plant engineers can read, review and revise. The system is strictly advisory, with every answer traced back to its sources. We also report organizational lessons from introducing agentic AI into a culture built on safety, traceability and conservative change. Beyond the technical architecture, the Beznau case study examines how an assistant can be introduced into a setting where evidence must be traceable, changes carefully reviewed, and operational decisions retained by plant personnel, paving the way for the responsible use of agentic AI in industrial plant monitoring.

new_items.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material
new_items.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly divide long tasks among subagents whose reports a senior agent turns into the final answer. Such a division of labor pays off only if each agent, and above all the senior agent, carries out the duties of its role. Current evaluations, however, mostly score the final answer, and a fluent, well-cited answer cannot show whether the senior agent weighed its subagents' reports or merely aggregated them. To assess whether a senior agent meets its assigned responsibilities, we define role integrity as the preservation of an agent's functional responsibilities when it acts on its subordinates' material. To measure it, we introduce RI-Bench, a behavioral benchmark grounded in the structures and public records of three institutional hierarchies: peer review, appellate adjudication, and parliamentary inquiry. We choose these hierarchies because their rules explicitly assign the senior role a duty toward subordinate material, and together they cover three basic duties: to weigh, to verify, and to relay. Rather than scoring output correctness, we measure how senior agents' outputs respond to controlled changes in subordinate material, using rule-based checks and a rubric-guided LLM judge calibrated against human annotation. Across eight LLMs and over 12,000 agentic episodes, senior agents rarely adopt a planted procedural error (2.9% of rulings) but often follow a majority of generic reviews (up to 71% of decisions) or drop witnesses' stated limitations (up to 65% of cited claims). Obligation prompts reduce these failures without removing them, and they also shift behavior in the control conditions. These findings motivate direct, obligation-specific evaluation of role integrity rather than inferring it from general capability or explicit role instructions. Code and data are available at https://github.com/jxtse/ri-bench.

new_items.title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain
new_items.summary: Language models fuse reports in retrieval, multi-agent consensus and agent memory, where treating shared-source reports as independent can double count evidence. A common remedy is an instruction to count each source once. Its value depends on the receiver's raw baseline. Pricing it needs an exact reference. We build the graded-dependence exact reference: binary worlds with single-report reliability 0.65 and four dependence levels, whose disclosed parameters give every world an exact posterior and every rule a target risk. The paired gain protocol scores raw and instructed answers of four configurations on 2,976 worlds. Agreement and gain separate in both directions. At $δ$ = 0, claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6.1-sol agreed with the rule within 0.001 in 744 of 744, and the instruction raised their posterior mismatch by 0.044; gpt-6-luna agreed in 165 of 744 and gained 0.0140 (95% interval 0.0064 to 0.0219); claude-haiku-5-5's gain moved from -0.0295 ($δ$ = 0) to +0.0302 ($δ$ = 1) (descriptive). The prespecified first-child endpoint contrast, gain at $δ$ = 1 minus $δ$ = 0, was 0.0342 (0.0303 to 0.0382). In the preregistered tests, the raw source-weight contrast was positive (0.259, 95% interval 0.182 to 0.337; Holm rejected zero) and the grouping endpoint difference was not detected (0.0004, -0.0023 to 0.0031). This interval excludes differences larger than 0.0031 in magnitude and lies within the registered precision bound of $\pm$0.0046. The reference prices the rule before any model call. The paired gain, estimable as a Brier difference on labelled deployment items, decides adoption per receiver and prompt condition.

new_items.title: Tracking and Limiting Unsupported Claim Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Provenance-Aware Framework
new_items.summary: This research examines how unsupported claims change as they move through multi-agent pipelines. It also examines whether preserving provenance can reduce these changes. We test both homogeneous and heterogeneous pipelines. Homogeneous pipelines use the same model across agents, while heterogeneous pipelines use different models. We compare the baseline with a provenance-aware framework. The framework passes each claim with its support status, source, evidence and transmission history. No new evidence is introduced during transmission. We measure changes in claim meaning, unsupported detail accretion, semantic drift, and provenance preservation. These metrics show whether the framework limits unsupported changes as claims pass between agents.

new_items.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
new_items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can infer private information from shared images, including locations, personally identifiable information (PII), and personal attributes such as age and sex, even from medical images. Adversarial perturbations can protect such information against black-box VLMs, but existing methods overlook image quality and introduce visible artifacts into the images they protect. We present SecretAgent, the first general multi-agent framework that protects image privacy against VLMs while preserving visual fidelity. LLM agents iteratively locate the visual evidence that reveals private information and adapt an invisible perturbation to the target VLM's answers and to an appearance reviewer agent, which rejects any candidate with visible artifacts. We instantiate SecretAgent with two complementary variants: SecretAgent-Gradient optimizes the perturbation through six surrogate encoders for cross-model transferability, and the gradient-free SecretAgent-Tool composes procedural noise and achieves the best perceptual fidelity on three of the five datasets. Experiments on four privacy applications (geolocation, PII, facial, and medical) across five datasets and six VLMs show that SecretAgent preserves image quality substantially better than existing methods while achieving state-of-the-art privacy protection in every application, and that its protection transfers to other VLMs.

new_items.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
new_items.summary: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or analysis code. Each agent has a defined responsibility within the workflow. An orchestrator plans the study; the LAMMPS and OVITO agents each use a generator-reviewer pair to prepare and review simulation and visualization scripts before execution; a high-performance computing agent dispatches jobs to remote resources; and an analysis agent interprets the completed run. The work- flow is accessible through a browser interface that streams thermodynamic data and rendered frames during local execution, allowing users to follow the simu- lation as it progresses. The architecture also supports new capabilities through loadable skills without modifying the agents, enabling autonomous hypothesis generation and testing. We evaluate ChatAtom through script-generation bench- marks, an end-to-end study of crack propagation, and a closed-loop campaign. By bringing script generation, execution, visualization, and analysis into one reviewed and observable pipeline, ChatAtom lowers the barrier to conducting MD studies and broadens access to advanced simulation workflows.

new_items.title: EvoTER: Evolving Embodied Agents via Tool-Use Experience and Reflection
new_items.summary: Long-horizon embodied tasks require agents to ground instructions in changing observations, coordinate heterogeneous tools, and recover from failures that can propagate through downstream operations. Although existing LLM-based agents retain experience and refine reusable skills, successful local repairs do not by themselves establish complete-task gains over the current shared procedure library. We present EvoTER, an experience-driven framework that enables embodied agents to self-evolve tool-use skills without updating model parameters. EvoTER operates through a three-role evolution loop: Explorer records tool-use trajectories; Diagnoser distills successful and failed executions into skills for tool selection, parameter computation, postcondition checks, and recovery; and Validator retains candidate revisions only when they improve complete-task success in fresh sessions. In simulation, EvoTER improves overall task success from a pre-evolution baseline of 53.60% to 80.40%. In real-world experiments, simulation initialization reduces the attempts required to acquire short-horizon skills, while continued real-world evolution improves long-horizon success from 20% to 80%-100% across tasks and enables the evolving skill library to incorporate new tool functionality introduced after simulation development. Project page: https://evoter-project.github.io/

new_items.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents
new_items.summary: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for cheap, high-throughput agentic deployment, but they remain weak at multi-step reasoning and tool use that long-horizon tasks demand. We study how to post-train an SLM to seek advice from a stronger model and act on that advice itself, following an advisor-executor pattern. Out of the box, this pattern fails across open- and closed-source small-model families: wiring an SLM to an advisor is a harness-design matter that is not enough on its own. A post-training recipe is needed to teach the model when to ask, in a cost-aware fashion, and how to follow advice across steps. Our method, ADAPT (ADvisor-Aware Post-Training), is a multi-stage recipe that instills this behavior, learning entirely from the policy's own rollouts supervised by the environment's outcome, with no learned reward model or human annotation. Across three domains, compared to an untrained harness baseline, ADAPT improves success rate in embodied text reasoning (TextWorld) from 24.5% to 77.3%, code generation (LiveCodeBench) from 21.8% to 56.0%, and deep web search (GAIA) from 17.5% to 49.3%, while querying the advisor sparingly (~1.0-2.1 calls per task). On the two long-horizon domains it closes 70-85% of the gap to an oracle that perfectly times when to ask for advice, and on code generation it exceeds that oracle. The gains persist when the advisor is replaced by one unseen in training, showing that the learned help-seeking policy is robust to a changing advisor rather than tied to the one it was trained with.

new_items.title: $γ$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
new_items.summary: Recent embodied agents construct and adapt robot behavior through executable programs, tool use, and interaction feedback. Studying these systems in mobile manipulation calls for physical worlds that connect agent-directed execution with its physical consequences and reusable interaction experience. We introduce $γ$-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform for mobile embodied intelligence. Agents compose motion tools and learned skills to carry out complete tasks that combine navigation and manipulation in a persistent physical world. BenchForge grounds structured objectives in physical task instances with instructions, reference programs, and goal evaluators, defining task goals while preserving agents' choice of valid solutions. An agentic collection harness further enables agents to produce demonstrations by carrying out contact-rich interactions through sustained control and physical feedback. Assisted reference execution and human guidance provide complementary experience. The resulting tool traces and aligned observation-action records support program refinement and policy learning, with common task-goal criteria for subsequent evaluation. We benchmark representative agent systems on complete tasks and demonstrate contact collection and trace-informed program revision. Together, these workflows provide infrastructure for research on embodied recursive self-improvement.

new_items.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
new_items.summary: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, the selected harnesses lead the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons, achieving 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench. Across three improvers and three edit scopes, from skill text to single-component and coordinated executable edits, GPT-6.1 Sol shows the largest average gain from the broadest scope. Our code is available at https://huangshengzebluesky.github.io/hookevo/.
